reviews.text:
Terrible news about a cat whose owner searched relentlessly for him. Turns out someone had hit it with their car and your vet practise had the cat the whole time and DIDNT CALL THE OWNER despite the cat being chipped and having had treatment with you in the past….
I wouldn’t trust this practise with a bargepole. Very dodgy.

My friend's 17-year-old cat Fudge was hit by a car on Friday 9 October. A local resident brought him to this practice the same day. Sadly, he died.

Over the weekend, my friend called the practice repeatedly, asking if a ginger cat had been handed in. Each time she was told nothing had been brought in. Meanwhile, she was searching for him and I was helping her make missing posters.

She was later told that staff had only checked the day logs, not the emergency logs.

When an owner calls about a missing pet, checking every log, including emergencies, should be basic. Because of this, she spent days searching for a cat that had already been brought here. I hope the practice fixes this so no other owner goes through the same thing.
Extremely kind and polite team.
Excellent surgery

I will absolutely Not be bringing my cat to this surgery ever again.

I attended for an emergency appointment on Nov 30th.
I was told she was given 3 injections to stabilise her and I was billed for them, but Im unsure when they actually did this. She was taken away for bloods, but when the vet came to update me on progress and results, she never said anything about administering stabilising drugs in the meantime.

When I asked for all of this info and blood test results to be sent to my local vets for further treatment, it took 2 phonecalls and me literally begging for it to be actually scanned and emailed.
If it weren't for the kind receptionist's persistence with the issue and reassurance, then I would've had a breakdown. Thank you Mikita/Nikita! You are the only redeeming factor of this surgery! (Sorry I didnt get your name, line wasnt great)

I had to book another emergency appt at my local vet 48hrs later as my cat was swaying and slipping on her back leg. However I was told by my local vet that what Streatham Hill has prescribed her was an opiod and she was having an adverse response to it.
Why didnt the vet at Streatham Hill ever mention this??

Fast forward 2 weeks and my insurance form Still has not been signed! My local vets not only signed it but sent the form in for me too!
After Both my insurance company and myself calling Streatham Hill Vets, I was informed there's a 2 MONTH DELAY in verfying insurance forms because the person who usually does it is 'off sick'.

GET IT TOGETHER.

I have a big note up in my kitchen to never seek help from this vet again.
Such wonderful staff and service. Our twenty year old cat gets first class treatment and the finest of care every time.
Four ⭐
I unreservedly thank the staff of Streatham Hill Veterinary Surgery for their exceptional care for my cat Caline.  Thanks!  :-)
👎 2 WEEKS - Vet won’t sign insurance claim after 4 EMAILS/3 Phone Calls/Whatsapp text - Still nothing.

My grandad was a vet, and I honestly thought I’d never find a veterinary practice that reminded me of the kind of service and care he built. But everyone here has been absolutely lovely and so caring.

They saved our little pup, and we honestly can’t thank them enough. The care, attention and kindness they showed him and us throughout was incredible. We are just so grateful to you all.

Thank you so much for everything you’ve done for him.

We really appreciate you 💙

I would highly recommend this vets to anyone.

Very mixed experiences as ever. The practice is very disorganised. I can book an appointment at 9am and be kept waiting for a very long time. There is always an excuse. Staff sickness, emergency, lack of consulting room etc. Every single time! I recently booked to pick up a post spay foster cat at 12.30pm and waited until 1.15pm. The receptionist spent nearly half an hour talking to a client at the desk about insurance admin and did not even let the nursing team know I had arrived. This is no longer my go to vets even though you are so close. I use several other local vets for my own cats and for other foster cats. None of them waste my time like this. We are all busy people with jobs and commitments.
This place literally saved my cats life thank you for everything daisy is thankful aswell!!
Such a wonderful surgery, everyone is always so lovely and makes it such a stress free visit!
Hi, Joe. We appreciate the rating, and are glad we could provide you with a positive experience!
Hi, Eva. We must have done something right to get such a good rating from you. We really appreciate you taking the time!
Friendly , thorough , caring vets , offer you different services and tells you the prices for you to choose.
I was not your client , but I had a emergency last Saturday, and you give me a support on that busy day that my guinea pig need! Thank you to all team for everything.

We changed our vets to Streatham Hill Vets after realising our cat had become increasingly traumatised by the treatment she was receiving in our (old) Norbury vets.
From the start Streatham Hill Vets were extremely understanding of her needs and absolute terror of going to the vets.
Rather than treating her as an inconveniently aggressive animal that needed to be treated in an inhumane, punitive manner, they actually empathised with & recognised the terrified creature she had become when faced with a visit to the vets.
Now our cat is a senior I feel much more confident that if there ever was a serious health issue she would be dealt with in a professional & caring manner.

I have had the worst experience with this vets. Left without clear communication and raised concerns with the head vet who called and spoke over me as i raised my worries. I havent been provided clear advice and the vets have not been clear about the options to me and not honest about what they have recommeded to me. I dont have any faith left and felt very little compassion in a difficult situation.

TRIGGER ALERT
My beloved dog Fendi died following a sudden and unexplained deterioration while receiving emergency veterinary treatment. I am seeking an independent investigation into the circumstances of her death and the care she received. I intend to make the findings public because I believe pet owners deserve transparency, accountability and confidence that their animals are safe when entrusted to veterinary professionals.

Fendi was admitted seriously ill with suspected parvovirus. At approximately 21:39 I was told her temperature had returned to normal and her vital signs were normal. Just 13 mins later — I was suddenly told her heart had stopped and CPR was underway.

I received no warning that she was deteriorating and no opportunity to get to her before she died.

I am now taking Fendi to the Royal Veterinary College for an independent post-mortem because I need to understand what happened during those final minutes, including what medication she received, the doses administered and how she was being monitored.

After her death, I personally removed the monitoring clips from her long-haired ears and observed that they appeared to be clipped onto her fur rather than making contact with the skin. I make no claim about the clinical significance of this — it is simply what I personally observed.

What has happened since is appalling. Despite repeated emails and WhatsApps concerning Fendi’s body and clinical records, nothing has been acknowledged. I have been told my emails have not even been opened and nobody will speak to me.

I have since read numerous other one-star reviews describing deeply concerning experiences, including one raising concerns about “oversedating”. I am not alleging this happened to Fendi — I will await independent evidence — but these accounts are extremely concerning to read.

I entrusted them with a little dog I adored. I was told her vital signs were normal and 13 minutes later her heart had stopped. Now I cannot even get an acknowledgement from them.

I will update this review when I have Fendi’s complete records and the independent post-mortem findings.

I would never want another owner to experience this.
Our first time and not the last!! Amazing people and a really good price also!! Very very good experience

I sadly had to put down my cat in August, which was dealt with well by the vets and staff. However I’ve called countless times, sent messages and even been into the surgery, they said they would get back to me the next day. Still nothing. This is really saddening as I couldn’t even afford to get her ashes and they know this. I just want to receive her paw print and fur cutting. Feels like a complete lack of care.

I can’t express my gratitude enough again to Streatham. The receptions are exceptional, nurses and Ivan too.. he shows exactly with animals the feeling of a paediatrician with kids how and why exactly how they will do their all to treat an individual thoroughly, and care so deeply. Such a remarkable vet who’s left me in great trust my baby is safe. This entire practice I know my cat is taken care of

I can’t recommend Streatham Hill Vets highly enough. They consistently provide such excellent care for my cats and have always been compassionate, friendly, knowledgeable and incredibly trustworthy. I always feel that my cats are genuinely cared for and that their wellbeing is the priority.

A special thank you to Ivan, who is a fantastic vet. He is kind and reassuring, and always takes the time to explain everything clearly and answer any questions. It makes such a difference knowing your pets are in such safe and caring hands.

Thank you to the whole team for the consistently wonderful care you provide!
Very helpful vet.  Kind and gentle
Ivan was brilliant - so insightful! Olive was very at ease.

Very poor experience with what should have been a simple case of conjunctivitis. My dog was given unsuitable medication, including an unnecessary painkiller with a hugely incorrect dosage on the label. Even at the correct dose, it made her vomit and couldn’t be used.

I called three times to request an alternative and received no response. I was eventually told a new medication was ready, only to arrive, be told they didn't have it, and the have to wait whilst they sorted it. I was also incorrectly told I owed money despite having already paid over the phone.

I sent a complaint email and was told nobody would respond for at least 21 days. Completely chaotic and frustrating. Almost £150 later, my dog still has conjunctivitis. I’ve completely lost confidence in the practice.
Really great service, seen quickly; staff are really knowledgeable and helpful. Thank you!

This is not a comment on any of the vets, nurses or reception staff, all of whom have been friendly and kind to my dog. However, this place is now so badly run that after nine years I'm moving my dog to a new surgery.

I recently had to take my dog in for a procedure to try to determine the cause of ongoing incontinence. The prospect was already distressing, because the potential causes are serious and leaving your dog at the vet is never nice. The experience was made far worse than it needed to be, for both of us.

On the day of the procedure, we were kept waiting 45 minutes beyond the 8.30am appointment time, then the relevant vet was not there to explain what was about to happen. I was told they'd call as soon as they arrived and that my dog would be ready to collect by 6pm. No call came, despite me leaving several messages. After an anxious day and no communication about delays, I finally heard from the vet at 6.30pm, then got my dog back at 8pm. He has a history of separation anxiety, so I was worried all day about his levels of distress.

I was told test results would take up to 10 days. I heard nothing for three weeks, despite calling and emailing. After going to the surgery in person, a vet finally rang me later that day. The delay was because of a filing mistake, which didn't explain the lack of reply to my emails. The results were not positive. The filing mistake has delayed me getting my dog the treatment he needs.

I'm so upset that this whole situation was poorly handled from beginning to end. I'm hoping for a better experience at my new vet.

Professional, prompt and understanding care. I would highly recommend Streatham Hill Veterinary Surgery after using their services due to an emergency last night.
Thank you Team
Hi, Sara. Thank you so much for rating your experience with us so highly!

I cannot thank the team at this veterinary surgery enough for everything they did for my 11-year-old African Grey parrot,Sammy. ❤️
When I brought him in, I was extremely worried and frightened, as he was very unwell and I genuinely didn’t know what the outcome would be. I though my Sammy will die . The team treated him with such care, professionalism and compassion, and they did everything they could to give him the best possible chance.
Their knowledge, dedication and attention to detail were truly exceptional. They took the time to explain everything to me, kept me informed throughout, and most importantly, they never gave up on him. Thanks to their expertise and incredible care, my parrot is still with me today.
When your pet is part of your family, having a veterinary team you can trust means everything. I will always be incredibly grateful to everyone who cared for him and helped save his life.
Thank you from the bottom of my heart for giving my beautiful boy another chance. I would wholeheartedly recommend this surgery to anyone looking for a veterinary team that genuinely cares about their patients.
My cat has been treated well there from the very beginning. Very friendly service. Best regards.

Shambolic service. My cat went in for a blood test (which I paid through the nose for), I didn't receive the results for almost two full weeks, despite chasing them three times. The third time I called I was transferred to a completely different branch by accident to a new vet who started talking to me about a dog. When I called back, the receptionist denied I had been transferred to anyone else. I was assured twice that the vet would call me that afternoon to explain the results - I'm still waiting. I won't be using them again. At time of writing I still don't know what is wrong with my cat and what treatment is needed. The trip to the vet for both of my cats cost me £343 on total. Avoid like the plague.

Edit: Here's an update to the above story. The manager called me and apologised for the treatment I received, and offered me a refund for the blood test, which I accepted. She then said a vet would be in touch, which happened. Then I was advised to have a telephone consultation for next steps and treatment, which was booked in for Saturday morning (today). I was told someone would call me at 10:45. I received no call so I decided to call them. At time of writing this edit, I am still on hold to them. It's been over ten minutes without anyone answering the phone. I cannot tell you how much you should avoid this veterinary surgery, they are an absolute shambles.
Great emergency overnight treatment

Appalling experience today. Registered early for a 14.45 appointment which was acknowledged and was told to take a seat until called. Waited 45 minutes and was told I hadn’t registered and all vets were all busy. Millie was only in to have her glands seen so offer was for a nurse to perform the procedure. Was then told there would be no charge but 15 minutes later I had a WhatsApp to say that I owed £50 + for a consultation ( not glands only which is normally circa £25). I returned to the clinic and was told records had been changed to show I owed nothing.

My observation is that as good as your vet’s are, reception is chaotic- this is an ongoing observation. For both receptionist to be on the phone dealing with enquiries is not providing good service for people looking to check in or pay for their visit. One receptionist said to a colleague she had been on the phone with just one customer for 29 minutes!

In my view this needs to be urgently addressed and much of not check in calls should be directed to someone who is qualified but on a separate phone line to the office on the first floor, rather than reception on the ground floor.
Very gentle with my cat<3
Emergency with my cat gone midnight amazing friendly caring staff unfortunately cat was too ill to survive caring and dignity to the end

Always a dream to take my dogs and puppies to Streatham vets.
Staff always friendly and welcoming
Love this vets. I feel lucky to have them.

I usually don't write reviews after one visit, because I feel as though there are many aspects of a day that can make a one-off visit seem bad when it is not a true reflection of the vet's standard care. However, the treatment I have gotten from Streatham Hill Vets has not only wasted my time and my money, but also prevented my dog from being treated somewhere else sooner.

Firstly, I called asking for estimates of a heart scan and a tooth extraction. I had to call, as they had not responded to either my text messages, my emails, or the website enquiry, which already raised red flags. After being on hold for around 15 minutes, I was verbally quoted around £450 for the scan and £600–£650 for the extraction (which was also consolidated by the prices I saw on their website). This was lovely to hear, as my usual vet had given me a quote nearly double that price. I wished to book my dog for a heart scan, but she needed a consult first (very understandable). The receptionist was kind and checked me in quickly. Whilst I was waiting, someone gave my dog a little treat which I found very thoughtful and kind. My appointment was at 3pm and I ended up being seen at around 3:15, which was a tad annoying but nothing too shocking.

What really confused me were the estimates I was given after the vet saw my dog. The £450 scan suddenly became £800, allegedly due to needing sedation. If that is the case, why was that not factored into the initial phone estimate? More shockingly, the £650 tooth extraction jumped to £1,100–£1,300. I was told it was classed as a "major" extraction (which is explicitly listed as £800 on their website), with the rest being "extra prices for the anaesthetic."

This makes no sense to me. Their own website explicitly states that their fixed-price dental bands fully include general anaesthesia and other necessary operational costs. When I called back to request an itemised PDF estimate to understand where this extra £300–£500 was coming from, the receptionist  verbally confirmed on the phone that the markup was indeed for anaesthetic and operational stuff.

Either their website is deliberately misleading and they are using (questionable at best, illegal at worst) drip-pricing tactics, which the government is actively cracking down on under the new Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act (DMCCA), or they are artificially hiking the price up for other reasons I am unaware of. Unsurprisingly, the next day they failed to send the itemised email they promised. In fact, they responded to my old email instead. For a 24 hour surgery, you’d think they’d be a bit more proactive in getting back to people. I’m not sure if they’re understaffed, but it really isn’t acceptable. I can only hope they aren’t this negligent to the pet owners who have their animals with them overnight.

I can't help but feel a bit conned. I checked their good reviews before booking a £50 consult that has now likely been rendered useless. Their lack of proper communication makes me feel as though they thought I would just pay nearly double the bill without a second thought. This whole situation has put me off this practice completely. It makes me seriously question whether they have the pets' best interests at heart, or if they are just another corporation trying to squeeze as much money out of people as possible. The staff were all wonderful, though, and my one star is solely for them. I cannot blame them for administrative decisions that are outside of their control.
Hi, Helen. We are delighted that you had a great experience with us. Thank you for taking the time to rate us!
Hi, Sevda. Your feedback is highly appreciated. Thank you so much for the review!

Absolutely disgusted with the experience our beloved dog and family have received by this veterinary surgery. Our dog was transferred from thier Wimbledon branch to Streatham for over night assistance due to respiratory issues, upon arrival our dog was clearly in respiratory distress while I was holding his oxygen tubes that needed to be connected to oxygen ASAP, we waited over 20 mins for a member of staff to come and check us in, considering the Wimbledon branch called ahead to say we were coming and gave them a full run down of the medical emergency our dog was having. After numerous attempts to get help, Tracey finally came out to see us, not at all interested in our dog or to ask us any questions but to hand us forms to sign and tell us the cost of an over night stay - my dog who was clearly struggling to breath at my feet was not even acknowledged! I repeatedly said he is insured, don’t worry about the cost we can cover it, please just help my dog. We were told, do not call us, we are very busy, no news is good news and the vet will call in the morning with an update, our response was, please call us if anything happens, it doesn’t matter what time of the night, just call us. We were not allowed in any further than the waiting room when he was then taken to the back. This was 7pm in the evening, the following morning after no news all night, at 8:30am a call from the vets came….. we’re sorry but your dog passed away this morning. In to much distress to talk, I ended the call and made my way straight to the surgery, arriving 25 minutes later, to be told the vet had gone home. That’s it, no explanation, no one knew what had happened to him - we were told the vet would call us the next day. The call never came, so I called the surgery, I was told the vet wasn’t working, I was read out a brief explanation of my dogs medical records by the receptionist and told to email the feedback team. I got a call one week later from Holly, very apologetic, told me the she will get the vet to call within a few days…. 2 weeks later, still no call. I called again to ask for the vet, the vet wasn’t there, I asked about my dogs ashes, apparently they were not back either, I called the cremation company, who told me they delivered the ashes 2 weeks prior back to the surgery. It then became apparent my dogs ashes were sitting in the office upstairs for 2 weeks and no one had bothered to call and let me know. I requested another call with Holly - that didn’t come either. Another email to ask for a call, and another and another to which I finally got a reply 6 days later. Holly again, very apologetic - then came the biggest shock, on my dogs medical records and medical costs that I requested were sent to me, right at the bottom in black and white - service provided:
*Euthanasia and Cremation*
I was told my dog died not that he was euthanised - Holly apparently could not see this on the medical records as they have a new system and said this isn’t the case, that my dog died but she was going to investigate. In the mean time she had a receptionist call me to discuss the insurance claim - while on the phone the receptionist went through the claim individually
*Euthanasia costs*
I said sorry, you’ve just said euthanasia, I need to speak to Holly, I was told he died not euthanised - she then said no I used the wrong words he did die - respiratory issues was the cause - she then said that she also couldn’t see anywhere on the records on the new system where it said euthanasia and asked me to send the records back, which I have done and guess what, no reply. So why has euthanasia been mentioned in the insurance claim?? In absolute despair, I am unable to talk to this team of people anymore. With still no phone call from the actual vet who was apparently looking after my dog that night until Monday 14th September apparently. Almost 5 weeks since he passed and no closer to the truth. Meanwhile I have to live with the guilt of leaving my beloved dog with these people who I thought were going to save him - I couldn’t have been more wrong.

We came in due to an emergency with our dog's stomach that had twisted, though at the time we had no idea at the time but wanted someone to look at her for she wasn't herself.
We had checked online (Google) on what the issue could be and thought rest would resolve the issue with our dog!
Having gone to previous emergency vet and the first thing your asked is if you have insurance, was so disheartening especially with how anxious and stressed we were. Leaving there disappointed we were worried for our dogs well being.
Then my sister reminded me that we had come across Veterinary Clinic website randomly a while back, and so we called to speak to a vet who told us to make our way down as quickly as possible.
The service from when we arrived, the initial check on and finally his decision to go ahead with the surgery to save our dogs life was beyond relief. Though the 4hr wait for the results of the surgery was gruesome and nerve racking ...........we waited in silence and tears, as we did not want to say goodbye to her this way.
Then the phone call came that she was out of surgery and in recovery, which made us all exhale as though we had been holding our breath. 59hrs later our girl came home and we will forever be grateful for the care that was given to her and us.

Thank you for seeing the need w came with and helped us first in ensuring her safety/health was priority.

Thank you
Hi, Zoe. We appreciate the rating, and are glad we could provide you with a positive experience!
So help ful and attentive service.  They really love the animals and helped my sweet cat.
Thoughtful,  caring staff. Really helped me with my poorly pooch
Very good vets they looked after my dog rosie Very well

I had an appointment to discharge my cat at 6pm, arrived at 6.10pm and was told by the receptionist/nurse at the desk that it could take a while due to emergencies. I was fine with this and waited, didn’t ask after my cat once. It came up to 9pm which is when I finally went to ask politely about her, the nurse at the desk was very friendly and went to the back to check and my cat was discharged almost immediately. A different nurse handed my cat back to me was not friendly, didn’t apologise and had a slight attitude with me. I had not spoken to her at all so not sure why she felt hostile towards me. The carrier was also not zipped up properly and my cat almost got out in the waiting room. When we brought her in she had made a mess in the carrier which was cleaned up but she had fecal matter on her which was still in the carrier on pick up. I usually have a good experience here and would not have been as upset by the delay if not for this rude nurse. I understand it’s an emergency vet but waiting 3 hours for a discharge feels like she was forgotten about and the dirty carrier shows a lack of care, a few puppy pads would have been appreciated especially when another patient was given blankets in their carrier to calm their anxious cat.

It’s a shame becauseI had an excellent experience here with my other cat. Seems they lack empathy for cats that are anxious which should be expected as they are unwell and in an unfamiliar environment.
Great experience, super friendly and super professional vets.

Vet service: not bad, not brilliant - my pet got fixed
Availability: obviously very good - it's 24 hours
Aftercare: very poor - consistently the bottleneck to my insurance claim (still waiting 4 months later for nearly £2k)

Brilliant surgery, excellent caring staff at reception and brilliant surgeons, both regular and locums (Mehmet from Old Registry). They have expert  knowledge and skill re surgery and post-surgery care. They were also patient and caring in times of crisis.
Always had a good experience at this vet surgery .. they are professional and always very kind and with our dog.

Great we found this 24h veterinary surgery. Open 24 hours. They have two parking spaces in front of the surgery, but please don't use them unless it is an emergency. We were in such a mind state when our beloved pet had an epilepsy seizure. Finding the space to park was (to us) a life saver. Do register with them. Non registered emergency visits, out of hours, could be expensive. The staff are really courteous. Genuinely. Night time we waited a long time, but at least we had them taking blood samples and even sold us cat treats that have a hole inside, for you to place pills, and it did make life easier for our cat to swallow the pill, otherwise difficult, as she eats the food and spit out the pills. Clever cats. One thing to consider when changing vets, as we did. Our vet just charged us for sending the cat's history to the new vet. if there's not enough stress in our lives. Worth considering going to them first, and requesting the papers in person. For us pet insurance is too late. This vet sells insurance. I guess it is worth considering this if your pet is not too old. For us it is too late. After the second seizure, i think it is time to consider the worse. Bless the poor thing.
The emergency care provided was excellent. Very friendly, reassuring staff, thorough vet and we left feeling confident that our dog would be ok. Thank you.
Great staff and top notch care!

Emailed, WhatsApp’d and called about cancelling a pet care subscription. All correspondence has been ignored. This coupled with the fact I have received no communication about the benefits in the plan since I signed up, point to this being a pure money grab.

I really appreciate the care and treatment my cat received from the veterinary team. However, I am extremely disappointed with the lack of support I have received when trying to claim back the cost of treatment through my insurance.

My insurer has advised me that the vet needs to submit the claim through their portal. I have called the practice seven times over the past month, and on each occasion I have been given assurances that it would be dealt with, only to receive no update or progress.

I have paid over £2,000 towards my cat’s treatment, and I am simply trying to recover what I am entitled to through my insurance. Throughout this process, I have remained patient, understanding and polite, as I appreciate that there may be backlogs. However, it is extremely frustrating to repeatedly chase this without receiving any meaningful help or even a clear update.

My cat received treatment over a month ago, and I feel it is unreasonable to have waited this long without the claim being submitted or being given a proper explanation for the delay.

While I am grateful for the clinical care my cat received, the handling of the insurance claim has been very disappointing. I sincerely hope the practice can improve its communication and follow-up with clients, particularly when significant amounts of money are involved.
Very good first impression. Considerate vets.

We recently had to put our beloved cat to sleep and I just wanna say massive thank you to the team. Especially Tracey - her kindness was so appreciated. I knew our little girl was going to be taken care of.

Will always be thankful for her compassion.

Bought my cat here as an emergency appointment. The vets lost blood test results and have failed to respond to my requests for information. I believe that they did not act in my cat's best interests. Our regular vet has taken our cat of the medication provided by this vet.
Appointment was late by 30min with no warning or explanation by reception.

This vet is a ripped off. We have been going there for several years but it is getting worst and worst. They don’t answer our emails, they charge us several times for follow up when asked to come back and despite us asking, they take ages to reply to the insurance… we have the feeling that they don’t care about the animals but want to monetize as much as possible. It’s time for us to change vets
Great efficient and good price

Not a good vets. First time veer using them claimed my pet was injured and that she needed surgery. Take her in on the day they said, they don't do surgery, rebook for surgery they don't do surgery because they say the bird has healed. When it was them who said the bird needed surgery in the first place. So just make up an issue to charge 200-300 odd quid. No one answers phones for 30 mins, no communication and i had to chase them up. Laughable

Had to use the emergency vet for our dog and they were so good - despite being absolutely rammed we were able to be seen relatively quickly and treatment given. The receptionists, nurses and vets were all up against it but were so professional and helpful.

The vets are lovely and they treat all pets with care, they are also very thorough at your appointment. There can be a delay in appointments and you will be on hold for a while if you call due to how busy they are, but that's expected of an emergency vets.

My main complaint is receiving results. My cat had a surgical biopsy two weeks ago due to weight loss + vomiting and I'm yet to receive those results. It's a shame because this surgery is so good at everything else, but watching my cat deteriorate because she's not being treated is really hard. I've contacted repeatedly and, if I do get an answer, I'm just told a vet will contact me, which hasn't happened.

Edit: I've had to submit a claim with the VCMS service as they have had the results for a week and still have not given them to me, wish I could give lower than one star. Avoid this place at all costs.

Been a VIP member for years and honestly starting to question what we pay for. We have been calling since July to try and get our dogs flea and worming treatment, and have been rushed of the phone every time, saying they would get it signed off with the vet that day… we’re still waiting I’ve currently been sat on hold for 20 mins as I attempt to chase… again.

Dear Sir/Madam,

I hope this email finds you well.

My name is Antonio, and I am Truffle’s owner.

Yesterday  I attended your clinic for Truffle’s dental check-up. My appointment was scheduled for 8:45 a.m.

I arrived early, as I am always punctual for my appointments. Unfortunately, I noticed that the same punctuality was not shown by your clinic. After waiting for 25 minutes, I decided to leave.

I do not consider it my responsibility if your clinic is experiencing scheduling issues or if your staff are unable to keep appointments running on time\. This is not the first time this has happened. The first time, I chose not to say anything, but this is now the second occurrence.

Just as I respect your time by arriving promptly, I expect the same respect in return. On the other hand, your clinic never delays charging for its services, and payment is always expected in full and without delay.

It is clear that there is a significant problem with the way appointments are managed. Appointments should be running on time, or at the very least no more than 5 to 10 minutes behind schedule. A client should not be expected to wait more than 10 minutes.

I am now reconsidering whether I will renew my annual subscription, as I no longer believe the level of service meets my expectations.

Once again, I urge you to address the ongoing issue with appointment scheduling and delays.

Yours sincerely,

Antonio

You know the feeling when your dog is ill and nobody will give you an answer? When he's lying by the door with no energy and you'd pay anything for one person to just take ownership of finding out what's wrong? That's where we were when we brought our Akita here.

We saw a different vet every single visit. Not once did the same person see him twice. Every single one of the 5 appointments so far, I started again from scratch — full history, from the top, to a stranger, while my dog stood shaking on the table wondering who this person was.

The last one graduated 8 months ago and was handed a complex case nobody had managed to diagnose. That's when it hit me: nobody here knows him. Nobody here is responsible for him. He's a slot in a diary.

Here's the part I still can't get my head around. In five weeks my dog has gone from 36kg to 32kg. That's over 10% of his bodyweight, gone, while under their care — and not one person at this practice has treated it as urgent. It's in their own records. Nobody has acted on it.

I complained multiple times over — I stopped counting at 5 approaches.

Each time I was promised a callback. Nobody has ever called back — not a vet, not a manager, nobody. Weeks later my phone still hasn't rung. A "caring local practice" that won't return calls from an owner with a sick dog.

Then I worked out why it feels this way. It isn't a local practice. It's a branch of the DNA Vetcare chain — same group as Peckham Veterinary Surgery, The Animal Clinic and Blackheath Veterinary Surgery, just different local names on the door. Check the footers yourself: Peckham Veterinary Surgery, The Animal Clinic and Blackheath Veterinary Surgery, just google :)

Their own website talks about "independence and integrity in veterinary care" and directors who are "visible and contactable". I couldn't get anyone to ring me back. It's laughable and I wish they would confront this fact but hey, profit is profit isn't it 😊

I'll be honest about why I'm writing this publicly: it's a cry for help. I've tried every private route and got nowhere, and this is the only way left to get anyone's attention. To the reception staff — I hope you'll forgive me. I know you're the ones who catch this, and I know the phones and the rota aren't your doing. You've been polite to me every time. My problem is with how this place is run, not with you. But I'm desperate, and I've run out of other options.

Your dog can't tell you when a practice has failed him. Mine couldn't. So I'll tell you instead: if your animal is genuinely ill, take him somewhere he'll be a patient and not a booking. We did. I only wish we'd done it weeks sooner.

I am extremely disappointed and upset by the treatment my 6-month-old puppy and I received yesterday.
I dropped my puppy off at 8:45am for a pre-booked spay operation. I was not contacted at any point throughout the day with any update. At 4:30pm, I had to chase the practice myself, only to be told that she had not yet had her operation but that she was “next”. An hour later, at approximately 5:30pm, I received a call informing me that they would no longer be able to spay her that day and that the procedure would have to be postponed until the following day.
I find this completely unacceptable. My puppy had been in their care since 8:45am, and I was given no update whatsoever until I contacted them myself. She had been fasted in preparation for surgery and had spent the entire day in an unfamiliar environment, waiting for an operation that ultimately was never carried out.
I understand that genuine emergencies can arise, and I appreciate that these may sometimes need to take priority. However, that does not excuse the complete lack of communication. Had I been contacted earlier, I could have collected my puppy and brought her home rather than leaving her there all day. If the practice does not have sufficient capacity or staffing to manage both pre-booked operations and emergencies, then I question why appointments are being booked in the first place.
When I went to collect my puppy, I was extremely upset and wanted to speak to a manager about what had happened. I was told that the management team would not see me. I was then offered a 20% discount if I chose to leave my puppy there for the operation the following day. I declined. There was no way I was going to leave her in their care overnight after the experience she had already been through.
I felt completely let down by the lack of communication, the way the situation was handled and the lack of accountability when I raised my concerns. I also felt that my concerns were not taken seriously.
My puppy will not be returning to this practice, and I have withdrawn her from their services. I would strongly urge other pet owners to consider how they would feel if their animal was left waiting all day for a procedure, with no communication from the practice, only to be told at the end of the day that the procedure had not taken place.

My cat started limping on the 15th May. I took him to a charitable vet initially as I thought he had just hurt his paw. That vet said he had a possible blood clot in his front left paw because it was pale and he had a cold leg and it was painful and they gave him metacam for pain and clopidogrel anti-platelet to try to dissolve the clot and sent us home with no follow up. He had been sedated because of an xray so he was out of it. I was so shocked that I took him to another vet initially Beckenham. They were dismissive and told me he was fine and that there was no clot but to keep giving the clopidogrel. I spent the night with so much anxiety I couldn’t sleep.

The next morning, I took him to Streatham Hill vets and this is where I finally felt heard and that he was being taken seriously. They explained he most likely has a clot and they needed to find the cause. He was kept overnight, had oxygen in the night and round the clock monitoring and started him on rivaroxaban (strong blood thinner) and continued to give clopidogrel but also gave him morphine for pain. They updated me constantly and I could call them anytime and they were super friendly and understanding. The next day they updated me further and explained everything I needed to do to ensure he was alright. They took bloods too. Following that they advised a heart scan and he was diagnosed with an enlarged left atrium (heart failure) which caused the clot in the heart to dislodge into his front arm. They liaised with the cardiologists and ensured he got the best care. Every time I called with a concern they were happy to see him the same day. They have been a God send and I truly believe he is still here because of them.

I know I don’t have long left with him, but they bought us precious time together than I probably would otherwise not have. I couldn’t thank them enough and recommend them enough! The prices are competitive too. They are not greedy and I always get the sense that they truly love the animals and treat them with upmost care and professionalism.
